# Hash-pinned install set for the LangGraph + OpenLLMetry OpenTelemetry recipe
# (examples/otel/langgraph/), run by ci.yml's otel-recipe-langgraph job.
#
# Direct requirements (the versions the recipe page records as verified):
#   langgraph==1.2.11 langchain-core==1.6.3
#   opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain==0.62.3
#   opentelemetry-sdk==1.44.0 opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0
#
# Installed into its OWN virtualenv in that job, never next to the dashboard.
# The recipe is what a user runs in their agent's process; the dashboard is a
# separate process. Keeping the two dependency sets apart means the check
# cannot pass only because the agent and ClawMetry happened to share a
# package, and it keeps LangChain out of every other job's environment.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses anything not
# listed here with a matching hash, so the whole closure is present. Each
# version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it.
#
# Regenerating by hand, resolved for the job's platform (Linux, CPython 3.11):
#   pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report r.json \
#     --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 --platform manylinux_2_17_x86_64 \
#     --platform manylinux_2_28_x86_64 --platform linux_x86_64 \
#     --python-version 3.11 --implementation cp --only-binary=:all: \
#     --target /tmp/t <the five direct requirements above>
# then, for each resolved name==version, take every sha256 under `urls` in
# https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json. Update the versions in
# examples/otel/langgraph/requirements.txt and docs/OTEL_RECIPE_LANGGRAPH.md in
# the same change: tests/test_otel_recipe_langgraph.py fails when they differ.
